title: 3-round AES-256: Three-round semi-square balance

target.description: 3 inner AES rounds, without initial whitening and with MixColumns in every round, under fixed round keys. The parameter-independent round argument applies to the standard AES-256 schedule.

setting.key_relation: 3 fixed round keys; the structural argument does not use key-schedule relations.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key restriction.
setting.plaintext_model: Fix every non-diagonal byte. Fix one chosen bit position in each of the four diagonal bytes and enumerate the other seven bits in each, giving 2^28 inputs.

time.note: Structural balance statement; the input cardinality is a property parameter.

success.description: A structural balance assertion, not a reported statistical attack-success rate.

evidence.locator: Printed p.126 AppendixA Proposition6 and following discussion
evidence.interpretation: Complete official eleven-page proceedings reviewed; critical equations and Table1 visually checked. Author-reported scope and native units retained.

evidence.locator: Complete PDF1–11/printed116–126; AppendixA Proposition6 and Sections4–5.
evidence.interpretation: Full exact-edition inventory reviewed; reviewer finite component validation is separate from attack reproduction.

limitations: Results are transcribed from this source version. Full attack searches, costs and success probabilities have not been reproduced.

Independent semi-square validation covers the algebraic balance, not random-permutation advantage, complete distinguisher cost or an attack reproduction. The two-fixed-bit failure is non-universal, not a claim that every smaller subset fails.

property.statement: After three inner AES rounds, the XOR of each output byte over the specified 2^28-input semi-square is zero.
property.quantifier: Source Proposition6 asserts bytewise balance for the full Cartesian set with one bit fixed in each diagonal byte, fixed passive bytes and fixed keys.
property.scope: One fixed bit position shared across four diagonal bytes; fixed values may differ. Fixing two bits is not universally balanced, but some restricted subsets can still balance.

parameters.name: Input structure size
parameters.meaning: Seven varying bits in each of four diagonal bytes.

parameters.name: Balanced outputs
parameters.meaning: Balance is asserted separately for each of the sixteen output positions.

validation.description: Proposition6 is stated in the source without a detailed derivation or empirical sample. The present local checker does not enumerate the 2^28-input structure. Fifth-batch reviewer supplies an independent parity-convolution argument using the two equal MixColumns coefficients: A*A=0 and A*Ac=0 for half-byte Sbox image sets. Finite checks cover32 convolutions and128 fixed-bit/value structures. A two-fixed-bit counterexample is computed by exact factorized byte marginals, not exhaustive2^28 evaluation.
